born.why: This code prioritizes survival by forcing the safe option 'a3' when danger (n1) exceeds 80, and using a more conservative fallback for moderate danger, while allowing the agent to pursue its default choice only when n1 is low enough to be safe.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding risky options (a1, a2) when danger (n1) exceeds 60, falling back to safer defaults (a3, a4), and aggressively reducing approach behavior to maintain a lower n1 baseline for longer-term persistence.

The previous code was overly cautious with arbitrary thresholds and hypothetical checks; this version simplifies the logic to rely on the default recommendation unless danger is critically high (>90), ensuring steady progress while preventing immediate death, as excessive hesitation can also be detrimental in many agent survival tasks.

The code prioritizes survival by lowering the retreat threshold to 80 and strictly limiting approaching items unless health is above 84, ensuring the agent avoids high-risk situations that could lead to death from n1 rising over time.

The code prioritizes survival by forcing a safe skip ('a4') when health (n1) is critical (>75) or when pending damage is disproportionately large relative to current health, ensuring the agent avoids fatal mistakes while still engaging with beneficial items when safe.

The revised code prioritizes survival by enforcing a hard stop at n1 > 90 and a cautionary skip if pending damage would leave the agent below 50 health or exceeds 30 points, preventing death from accumulated risk while still allowing actions when health is high.

This code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding actions that increase risk when `n1` is high or history indicates danger, and only accepts slight risks in safe zones, while simplifying approach to prevent unnecessary exposure.

This code dynamically evaluates the safety of each option based on historical data (`z`), penalizing options that led to high danger levels and preferring those associated with lower `n1`, thereby adapting to the agent's specific risk profile rather than relying on static defaults.
